classification.difficultyReason: Model an open cylindrical pool, combine its floor and wall areas, convert tile dimensions and estimate a tile count.

content.prompt: A circular swimming pool has a diameter of $10\text{ m}$ and is $1.3\text{ m}$ deep. The interior of the pool was covered with square tiles of side length $2\text{ cm}$. Approximately how many tiles were required? Give your answer to the nearest hundred tiles.

answer.short:
About $298\,500$ tiles.

Combine the circular floor area and the curved wall area, then divide by the area of one tile.
answer.worked:
The interior consists of the circular floor and the cylindrical wall. Unrolling the wall gives a rectangle whose length is the pool's circumference and whose width is its depth.

$$\begin{align*}r&=10\div2=5\text{ m}\\A_{\text{floor}}&=\pi\times5^2\\A_{\text{floor}}&=25\pi\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{wall}}&=(2\pi\times5)\times1.3\\A_{\text{wall}}&=13\pi\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{interior}}&=25\pi+13\pi\\A_{\text{interior}}&=38\pi\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

Each tile has side length $2\text{ cm}=0.02\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{tile}}&=0.02^2\\A_{\text{tile}}&=0.0004\text{ m}^2\\N&=\frac{38\pi}{0.0004}\\N&=95\,000\pi\\N&\approx298\,451.30\end{align*}$$

Approximately $298\,500$ tiles were required, rounding to the nearest hundred.
